title: Foreign Area Officer Indo-Pacific (I) (Gen to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
13. MOS 8243, Foreign Area Officer Indo-Pacific (I) (Gen to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC
PP&O

    a. Summary. Foreign Area Officers are officers who have completed
graduate-level study of international relations, with an emphasis in regional
studies appropriate to a designated region, are proficient in a foreign
language and who have extensive in-country experience in a designated region.
This MOS may be assigned only as a FMOS. It will be assigned and voided only
by the authority of CMC (MM).




                                         1-337                       Enclosure (1)
 1145                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have broad travel experience in the designated region.

        (2) Security requirement: TS/SCI security clearance eligibility
based on a tier 5 background investigation.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) FAOs must certify their language proficiency annually in two of
three modalities (listening, reading, speaking) through the Defense Language
Proficiency Test and Oral Proficiency Interview. FAOs who certify through
the authorized testing procedures at or above the ILR proficiency level of
three in two of three modalities may recertify every 2 years.

        (2) Display extensive knowledge of a designated region to include
military forces, culture, history, sociology, economics, politics, and
geography.

    d. Duties. Performs in operational and strategic level Marine Corps,
joint, or combined staffs in operations, planning, security cooperation, or
intelligence billets; or within the Defense Attaché System (DAS).

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Political Scientists 19-3094.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
